confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web search summaries of cost-of-living aggregators: Numbeo (Oct 2026), Livingcost (Jul 2026), Expatistan (Sep 2026) and Hikersbay. Typical figures were a domestic draft beer at about EUR 2.5-3.0, a cappuccino at about EUR 2.6-3.2, an inexpensive meal at about EUR 9-10 and a mid-range three-course dinner for two at about EUR 50-60. I converted to USD at roughly 1.10 USD per EUR. That rate is implied by third-party figures quoted from the RBA's 18 Nov 2026 rates, which are later than the July 2026 pricing window. Cocktail prices vary widely: about EUR 6 in a crowd-sourced figure based on few data points, EUR 8-12 at a classic bar, and EUR 12-18 at rooftop bars. I used about EUR 9 as a typical restaurant or bar cocktail. The wine figure is weakly sourced: one Old Town wine bar at about EUR 4.50 per glass, cross-checked against the local beer price ratio. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July high season from general knowledge. I did not check accommodation prices or listings, so they are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate comes from a search summary that pointed to the RBA exchange-rates pages.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink are based on aggregated Bratislava price indexes. Accommodation is benchmarked against Central European capitals with moderate tourist demand, roughly between Budapest and Ljubljana. Bratislava is usually a little cheaper than Vienna and Prague but has a smaller supply of hostels.
